description: Search performance for ONE page URL (an article, landing page or side page): per-provider `totals` (clicks, impressions, ctr, position) from Google Search Console and Bing, the top `queries` it gets impressions for (Google Search Console only; clicks, impressions, ctr, position per query), a weekly `timeseries` ({dates, clicks, impressions, position} columnar arrays), `ga4` landing-page engagement (sessions, engagementRate, avgEngagementTime in seconds, keyEvents, aiReferralSessions), and `bingAiCitations` (Copilot citation snapshots for that page). Pass the page's full `url`; http/https, www, trailing slash and tracking params are matched either way. Sections that are not stored for the page come back null, and `notes` says why (no connection, page not in the synced top pages, no AI-citation import). Bing grounding queries are not stored per page, so `bingAiCitations.groundingQueries` is always null; use `search_ai_citations` for site-wide ones. Reads already-synced data only. Free. Use it before refreshing an article to see which queries it ranks for and where it sits, whether impressions are trending up or down, and whether AI assistants cite it. Use `search_performance` for site-wide numbers. `days` is 7, 28, 90, 180 or 480 (default 90); `limit` caps `queries` (default 50, max 200).

days.description: Lookback window in days: 7, 28, 90, 180, or 480. Default 90.

limit.description: Max queries returned, top by impressions (default 50, max 200).

url.description: Full URL of the page, e.g. https://example.com/blog/my-article

name: search_page_performance
